Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-medium-0140", "row_sha256": "cd255dd44fcc086628e6150329a0b111893cd004189370a0d85f03952ebd0433", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you review this one entry from our rehearsal recording archive and tell me what metadata might need attention? this is the full note i have: “North Room, 14 March 2024; Glass Orchard; rehearsal, not a live show; files named GO_0314_A.wav and GO_0314_B.wav; A is 48 kHz/24-bit mono, B is 44.1 kHz/16-bit stereo; the handwritten sheet says ‘second run, after the pause’; no performer names are written down. The folder title is ‘Glass Orchard March’.” I’m not asking you to listen to the files or guess who played. Please stick to this entry and the details in the note, and don’t fill in missing names or decide which file is better. I mainly need a short numbered checklist of possible metadata issues to check, not a rewritten catalog record. For each point, put the detail from my note first, then say what question or follow-up it suggests. If something looks fine or there isn’t enough information to flag an issue, say that plainly rather than making up a problem. Keep the distinction between what the note actually says and what you’re asking us to verify. thanks", "output": "Review the single rehearsal-archive entry below and provide a short, numbered checklist of possible metadata issues to check. Use only the information in the note; do not listen to the files, guess performer names, choose a preferred file, or rewrite the catalog record.

For each checklist item, state the relevant detail from the note first, then give the question or follow-up it suggests. Clearly distinguish recorded facts from questions to verify. If a detail appears fine or there is not enough information to flag an issue, say so plainly rather than inventing a problem.

Entry note: “North Room, 14 March 2024; Glass Orchard; rehearsal, not a live show; files named GO_0314_A.wav and GO_0314_B.wav; A is 48 kHz/24-bit mono, B is 44.1 kHz/16-bit stereo; the handwritten sheet says ‘second run, after the pause’; no performer names are written down. The folder title is ‘Glass Orchard March’.”"}]
